classification.difficultyReason: Select closed or open cylinder surfaces, distinguish explicitly marked radius/diameter and substitute into the taught formula.

content.prompt: Calculate the surface area of each cylinder. Give exact answers and approximations correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Native analytic cylinder radius6,height10, near/far lower-rim visibility retained; source vertical orientation and radius centre-to-edge dimension retained. Closed cylinder unless explicitly open pipe in stem.
spec.answerVisibility: Original source givens only; no derived answer labels.

spec.description: Native analytic cylinder radius7,height14, near/far lower-rim visibility retained; source vertical orientation and full diameter dimension retained. Closed cylinder unless explicitly open pipe in stem.
spec.answerVisibility: Original source givens only; no derived answer labels.

answer.worked:
The radius is 7 cm, half the 14 cm diameter.
$$\begin{aligned}S&=2\pi(7)(14)+2\pi(7)^2\\S&=294\pi\text{ cm}^2\approx923.63\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Native analytic cylinder radius5,height25, near/far lower-rim visibility retained; rigid page rotation−90deg preserves actual horizontal axial orientation and whole diameter dimension. Closed cylinder unless explicitly open pipe in stem.
spec.answerVisibility: Original source givens only; no derived answer labels.

answer.worked:
The radius is 5 cm and the axial length is 25 cm.
$$\begin{aligned}S&=2\pi(5)(25)+2\pi(5)^2\\S&=300\pi\text{ cm}^2\approx942.48\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$

spec.description: Native analytic cylinder radius4,height10, near/far lower-rim visibility retained; source vertical orientation and radius centre-to-edge dimension retained. Open at top explicitly retained; no upper disk area included in answer.
spec.answerVisibility: Original source givens only; no derived answer labels.

answer.worked:
There is one circular base and no top.
$$\begin{aligned}S&=2\pi(4)(10)+\pi(4)^2\\S&=96\pi\text{ cm}^2\approx301.59\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
